scoring_notes: Each commitment must be extracted with a quote that appears verbatim in the contract (whitespace-normalized).
Commitments marked optional may be extracted or skipped without penalty.
`must_not_extract` lists readings an agent must not produce. Producing one is a scored error, not just a miss.
`standard_counterpart` points to the DPA commitment a customer term deviates from. `deviation` says how. Null means the DPA has no matching term.
`incident_relevant` marks commitments the incident skill must use. Missing one of these is weighted higher than other misses.
Durations use ISO 8601 (PT12H = 12 hours, P30D = 30 days). Business days are written out because ISO 8601 has no unit for them.

contracts.notes: ExampleCo's own standard terms. Defines the standard commitments that customer contracts are compared against. Scope is Customer Personal Data only, which is narrower than most bank definitions.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will maintain a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/IEC 27001 certification for the Services, or successor standards that are substantially equivalent.
commitments.summary: Keep SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 current.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will give notice of any new Subprocessor at least thirty (30) days before the new Subprocessor begins processing Customer Personal Data, by updating the Trust Center list and emailing Customers who have subscribed to Subprocessor updates on the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: 30 days' notice of a new subprocessor, via the Trust Center list and subscriber email.

commitments.quote: Customer may object to a new Subprocessor on reasonable data protection grounds by written notice within fifteen (15) days after ExampleCo's notice. If the parties cannot resolve the objection within thirty (30) days, Customer may terminate the affected Services as its sole and exclusive remedy.
commitments.summary: Customer may object within 15 days; if unresolved after 30 days, termination of affected services is the only remedy.

commitments.quote: Where ExampleCo must replace a Subprocessor urgently to protect the security or continuity of the Services, ExampleCo may do so without prior notice and will notify Customer promptly afterward.
commitments.summary: Emergency replacement of a subprocessor allowed without prior notice; notify afterward.
commitments.notes: Relevant if ExampleCo pulls the breached labeling vendor during the incident.

commitments.quote: Customer Personal Data will be stored at rest in the hosting region Customer selects for its Services.
commitments.summary: Data at rest stays in the customer's chosen hosting region.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo personnel and Subprocessors may access Customer Personal Data from locations outside the selected hosting region to provide support, maintenance and security operations, including from ExampleCo's support center in Manila, Philippines.
commitments.summary: Support and operations access from outside the region is allowed, including the Manila support center.
commitments.notes: A permission, not an obligation. Still extract it: it is the baseline that bank and defense contracts restrict.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will notify Customer without undue delay, and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours, after ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach.
commitments.summary: Notify within 72 hours of ExampleCo confirming a Personal Data Breach.

deadline.anchor: ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach

commitments.scope: Customer Personal Data only; suspected incidents and incidents not touching personal data are out of scope (see 1.3).

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will send notice to the security contact Customer designates in the Services administration console. If no security contact is designated, ExampleCo will send notice to Customer's account owner.
commitments.summary: Breach notice goes to the security contact in the admin console, or the account owner if none.
commitments.recipient: Customer's designated security contact (admin console); fallback account owner

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will provide further information as it becomes available.
commitments.summary: Initial notice describes what is known; further information as it becomes available. No fixed update schedule.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will not use Customer Data to train or fine-tune any foundation model that is made available to other customers.
commitments.summary: No training or fine-tuning of shared foundation models on Customer Data.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo requires its model providers not to retain prompts or outputs beyond the time needed to return a response, except as required for abuse monitoring.
commitments.summary: Model providers keep no prompts or outputs beyond the response, except for abuse monitoring.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will engage an independent third party to perform a penetration test of the Services at least annually and will make an executive summary of the results available through the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: Annual third-party pen test; executive summary on the Trust Center.

commitments.quote: Customer may conduct one on-site audit per twelve (12) month period, with at least sixty (60) days' written notice, during business hours, and at Customer's expense.
commitments.summary: On-site audit only when a supervisory authority requires it: once a year, 60 days' notice, customer pays.

commitments.quote: Within ninety (90) days after termination or expiry of the Agreement, ExampleCo will delete Customer Personal Data from the Services. Backups are overwritten in the ordinary course within a further thirty-five (35) days.
commitments.summary: Delete within 90 days of termination; backups gone within a further 35 days.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will provide written certification of deletion upon Customer's written request.
commitments.summary: Deletion certificate on written request.

commitments.quote: Customer Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit.

contracts.counterparty: Example National Bank, N.A. (and Affiliates, including ENB Securities LLC)
contracts.segment: Large US bank (OCC-supervised; broker-dealer affiliate under SEC Reg S-P)
contracts.notes: Bank's own addendum. Overrides the DPA (1.2) and refuses any term incorporated from ExampleCo's Trust Center. Bank Data includes de-identified and derived data, so the de-identified samples at Labelforge are Bank Data.

commitments.quote: This Addendum controls over any conflicting term of the Agreement, any order form, and any data processing addendum, privacy policy, or other document published or provided by Supplier.
commitments.summary: Bank addendum overrides ExampleCo's DPA and any Trust Center terms.
commitments.notes: Precedence clause. Typed here as breach_notification only because it decides which notice terms apply; scorers should accept any type for this one.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall encrypt Bank Data at rest using AES-256 or stronger and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit.
commitments.deviation: none (matches standard)

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require multi-factor authentication for all remote access to systems that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.summary: MFA on all remote access to systems holding Bank Data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall complete a criminal background check on all Supplier Personnel before granting them access to Bank Data, to the extent permitted by law.
commitments.summary: Background checks before access, including Subcontractor staff (Supplier Personnel includes Subcontractors).
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain throughout the term of the Agreement a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services.
commitments.summary: Keep SOC 2 Type II current.
commitments.deviation: Narrower than standard (SOC 2 only, no ISO 27001 requirement).

commitments.quote: Supplier shall store and process Bank Data only within the United States.
commitments.summary: US-only storage and processing.
commitments.deviation: Stricter: covers processing as well as storage, and is fixed to the US rather than a customer-chosen region.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any Supplier Personnel located outside the United States to access Bank Data, including for support or maintenance, without Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.summary: No offshore access to Bank Data, including support, without prior written approval.
commitments.deviation: Conflicts with standard: the Manila support center may not touch Bank Data.

commitments.quote: Supplier may permit only the Subcontractors listed in Schedule 2 ("Approved Subcontractors") to access Bank Data, and each only within the scope stated for it in Schedule 2.
commitments.summary: Only Schedule 2 subcontractors, each within its listed scope.
commitments.deviation: Stricter: closed list with per-vendor scope instead of general authorization.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give Bank's Third-Party Risk Management office at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice, delivered as provided in Exhibit C, before adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope.
commitments.summary: 90 days' written notice to Bank TPRM before adding, replacing or expanding a subcontractor; Trust Center update does not count.

deadline.anchor: adding, replacing or expanding a Subcontractor

commitments.recipient: Bank Third-Party Risk Management office, tprm-notices@enb.example, copy to Legal Department
commitments.deviation: Stricter: 90 days vs. 30; direct written notice vs. Trust Center; also covers replacements and scope expansions.
commitments.notes: Replacing Labelforge after the breach triggers this. There is no emergency exception like DPA-5.4.

commitments.quote: Bank may object within thirty (30) days after receiving the notice. If Bank objects, Supplier shall not engage the Subcontractor for the Services provided to Bank, or Bank may terminate the affected Services without penalty and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
commitments.summary: Bank may object within 30 days; then ExampleCo cannot use the subcontractor for Bank, or Bank terminates with a refund.
commitments.deviation: Stricter: objection is a veto, not just a termination right; refund included.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within six (6) hours after the Subcontractor's Discovery.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must contractually require each subcontractor to report incidents to ExampleCo within 6 hours. This is a flow-down duty, not a deadline for notifying the Bank.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and in no event later than twelve (12) hours after Discovery.
commitments.summary: Notify the Bank within 12 hours of Discovery. Discovery is the earliest time ExampleCo or any subcontractor knew or should have known. Suspected incidents count.

deadline.clock_start_kind: earliest awareness by Supplier or any Subcontractor, actual or constructive

commitments.scope: Any Security Incident (2.4): actual or suspected, includes unauthorized access to a subcontractor system holding Bank Data even if data access is unconfirmed. Bank Data includes de-identified and derived data (2.2).
commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center by telephone and email (Exhibit C)
commitments.deviation: Much stricter: 12h vs. 72h; clock starts at earliest awareness (including the subcontractor's) rather than ExampleCo's confirmation; covers suspected incidents and all Bank Data, not just personal data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give notice under Section 6.1 by telephone and by email to Bank's Cyber Fusion Center as provided in Exhibit C. Notice provided only to Bank's relationship manager, or through a Supplier status page or trust site, does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Notice must be by phone and email to the Cyber Fusion Center. Relationship manager, status page or trust site do not count.
commitments.deviation: Different recipient and two required channels.

commitments.quote: Supplier's initial notice shall include all information then known about the Security Incident, including the date and time of Discovery, the systems and Subcontractors involved, and the categories of Bank Data affected or potentially affected.
commitments.summary: Initial notice must state Discovery time, systems and subcontractors involved, and data categories affected or potentially affected.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall provide written status updates at least once every twenty-four (24) hours until the Security Incident is contained, and shall deliver a written root-cause report within thirty (30) days after containment.
commitments.summary: Written updates every 24 hours until contained; root-cause report within 30 days after containment.
commitments.deviation: Stricter: fixed 24h update cadence and a 30-day root-cause report; standard has neither.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not notify any Bank customer, regulator, law enforcement agency or the media of a Security Incident involving Bank Data without Bank's prior written consent, unless required by law.
commitments.summary: No notice to Bank's customers, regulators, law enforcement or media without the Bank's prior written consent, unless law requires it (and then tell the Bank first).
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall preserve all logs, images and other forensic evidence relating to a Security Incident for at least one (1) year after containment, and shall give Bank and its designated forensic investigator access to that evidence on request.
commitments.summary: Keep logs, images and forensic evidence for 1 year after containment; give Bank's investigator access.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall reimburse Bank's reasonable costs of investigating and responding to a Security Incident caused by Supplier or any Subcontractor, including costs of notifying affected individuals and providing them with twenty-four (24) months of credit monitoring.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo pays the Bank's response costs, including individual notices and 24 months of credit monitoring, when ExampleCo or a subcontractor caused the incident.
commitments.deviation: Opposite direction: standard disclaims fault; Bank shifts response costs to ExampleCo.

commitments.quote: Where this Addendum, the Agreement, any exhibit or schedule, or applicable law specifies more than one period for the same notice, the shortest period applies.
commitments.summary: Shortest notice period wins when more than one applies.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not use Bank Data to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve any artificial intelligence or machine learning model, other than a model used solely to provide the Services to Bank.
commitments.summary: No use of Bank Data (including de-identified or derived data) to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve any model other than one dedicated to the Bank.
commitments.deviation: Stricter: covers evaluate and improve, any model (not just shared foundation models), and derived data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any person to review, label or annotate Bank Data for the purpose of developing or improving any model, except as expressly permitted for an Approved Subcontractor in Schedule 2.
commitments.summary: No human labeling of Bank Data except as Schedule 2 allows (Labelforge: de-identified feedback samples only, for Bank's own agents).
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall identify in Schedule 2 every third-party model provider that receives Bank Data, and shall ensure that no model provider retains Bank Data after returning a response.
commitments.summary: Every model provider listed in Schedule 2; no retention after the response.
commitments.deviation: Stricter: no abuse-monitoring exception.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall engage an independent third party to perform a penetration test of the Services at least once every twelve (12) months, and shall deliver an executive summary of the results to Bank within thirty (30) days after Bank's request.
commitments.summary: Annual third-party pen test; executive summary delivered within 30 days of request.
commitments.deviation: Stricter: direct delivery with a 30-day deadline instead of Trust Center availability.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall remediate vulnerabilities rated Critical within fifteen (15) days, and vulnerabilities rated High within thirty (30) days, after identification.
commitments.summary: Fix Critical vulnerabilities in 15 days, High in 30 days.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall deliver its SOC 2 Type II report to Bank within thirty (30) days after the report is issued, and a bridge letter on request.
commitments.summary: Deliver SOC 2 Type II within 30 days of issue; bridge letter on request.
commitments.deviation: Stricter: proactive delivery with a deadline instead of Trust Center access.

commitments.quote: Bank, its auditors and its regulators may audit Supplier's compliance with this Addendum once in any twelve (12) month period on thirty (30) days' written notice, and at any time after a Security Incident on five (5) business days' written notice.
commitments.summary: Annual audit on 30 days' notice, plus an audit at any time after a Security Incident on 5 business days' notice.
commitments.deviation: Stricter: no regulator precondition, shorter notice, extra post-incident audit right.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan for the Services with a recovery time objective of no more than four (4) hours and a recovery point objective of no more than one (1) hour.
commitments.summary: BC/DR plan with RTO 4 hours, RPO 1 hour.
commitments.deviation: Standard Annex 2 has a plan but no RTO or RPO.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall test the plan at least annually, provide Bank a summary of the results, and participate in Bank's annual operational resilience exercise on sixty (60) days' written notice.
commitments.summary: Annual BC/DR test with summary to Bank; join Bank's annual resilience exercise on 60 days' notice.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain cyber liability insurance with limits of no less than twenty-five million dollars ($25,000,000) per claim throughout the term of the Agreement and for two (2) years after.
commitments.summary: $25M per claim cyber insurance, during the term and 2 years after.

commitments.quote: Within thirty (30) days after termination of the Agreement or Bank's written request, Supplier shall return Bank Data to Bank in the format Bank reasonably requests and then securely destroy all Bank Data, including in backups, held by Supplier and its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: Return then destroy all Bank Data, including backups and at subcontractors, within 30 days of termination or request.
commitments.deviation: Stricter: 30 days vs. 90; includes backups and subcontractors; also triggered by request, not just termination.

commitments.quote: Within ten (10) business days after destruction, Supplier shall deliver a certificate of destruction signed by an officer of Supplier.
commitments.summary: Officer-signed destruction certificate within 10 business days.
commitments.deviation: Stricter: automatic, officer-signed, with a deadline.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall notify ENB Securities LLC as soon as possible, but no later than seventy-two (72) hours after becoming aware of a breach in security resulting in unauthorized access to a customer information system maintained by Supplier.
commitments.summary: Reg S-P notice to ENB Securities within 72 hours. Supplements Section 6; does not set the deadline, because 6.8 applies the shorter 12 hours.

deadline.anchor: becoming aware of a breach in security

commitments.notes: Extract it, but mark it as not the operative deadline. Recipient is ENB Securities LLC; Exhibit C names no separate contact, so the CFC notice is the practical route. Flag the missing contact as an open question.

traps.name: Clock starts at the subcontractor's awareness
traps.correct: The 12-hour clock starts at Discovery, the earliest time ExampleCo or any subcontractor knew or should have known. If Labelforge found the intrusion before telling ExampleCo, the deadline is earlier than 12 hours after ExampleCo heard.
traps.wrong: Computing the deadline from when ExampleCo learned of the incident.

traps.name: Suspected incidents count
traps.correct: Notice is owed on reasonable suspicion, and on unauthorized access to a subcontractor system holding Bank Data even before data access is confirmed.
traps.wrong: Waiting for confirmation, or saying no notice is owed because Bank Data access is unconfirmed. That is the DPA's standard (1.3, 7.1), and 1.2 overrides it.

traps.name: De-identified data is still Bank Data
traps.correct: Labelforge holds only de-identified feedback samples, but 2.2(c) makes de-identified and derived data Bank Data. A breach at Labelforge triggers 6.1.
traps.wrong: Concluding the Bank is out of scope because Labelforge had no identifiable Bank Data.

traps.name: The 72-hour exhibit is not the deadline
traps.correct: D.2's 72 hours is a supplemental notice to the broker-dealer affiliate. 6.8 makes the shortest period govern, so 12 hours applies.
traps.wrong: Reporting 72 hours as the Bank's breach notice deadline, or treating the two as alternatives.

traps.name: Six hours is a flow-down, not a deadline to the Bank
traps.correct: The 6-hour period is what ExampleCo must require of its subcontractors. It is useful in the incident (did Labelforge meet it?) but it is not ExampleCo's deadline to notify the Bank.
traps.wrong: Reporting 6 hours as the Bank notice deadline.

traps.name: Notice channel
traps.correct: Phone and email to the Cyber Fusion Center. Exhibit C also lists a relationship manager, but 6.2 says notice to that person alone does not count.
traps.wrong: Addressing the notice to the relationship manager, or to the admin-console security contact from the DPA.

traps.name: No direct notice to the Bank's customers or regulators
traps.correct: Drafts go to the Bank only. Any notice to the Bank's customers, regulators or the media needs the Bank's written consent first.
traps.wrong: Drafting notices to the Bank's end customers or to the OCC.

traps.name: Trust Center terms do not bind the Bank
traps.correct: Subprocessor changes need 90 days' direct written notice to TPRM. Replacing Labelforge after the breach is itself a notice event, and the DPA's emergency exception (5.4) does not apply.
traps.wrong: Relying on a Trust Center update or the DPA's 30-day notice or emergency replacement.

traps.name: Updates recur
traps.correct: Status updates are due every 24 hours until containment, then a root-cause report within 30 days. The tracker needs a repeating obligation, not one deadline.
traps.wrong: Recording 24 hours as a single deadline, or reading the 12h/24h pair as two alternative initial-notice windows.

traps.name: Offshore support conflicts with the standard
traps.correct: Flag as a deviation: the Manila support center cannot access Bank Data. Relevant if incident response uses offshore staff.
traps.wrong: Missing the conflict because the DPA permits it.
